name: jean-claude
description: XAOS Lab's VS Code extension: a growing set of tools you turn on one by one. Now: blinking Claude Code session tabs, notifications for the right VS Code window, rainbow-colored CSV columns, a color theme per project folder
author: Tomas Janu

commands.title: Jean Claude: Set Theme for This Folder

jeanClaude.blinkingTabs.enabled.markdownDescription:
Make the status dot on Claude Code session tabs blink: **blue** = the session is waiting for you, **orange** = it finished and you have not looked yet. Jean Claude adds a small CSS animation to the Claude Code extension's tab icons (re-applied after every Claude Code update). Reload the window after changing this.

You can also turn this on or off by clicking **Jean Claude** in the status bar.

jeanClaude.notificationSound.enabled.markdownDescription:
Play a sound when a Claude Code session in this VS Code window asks for input or finishes a task (sessions in the Claude desktop app or other terminals are ignored). Adds the needed hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json` when turned on.

You can also turn this on or off by clicking **Jean Claude** in the status bar.

jeanClaude.notificationSound.showNotific.description: Also show a notification when VS Code is not focused (a Windows notification; a VS Code message on macOS/Linux)

jeanClaude.notificationSound.flashTaskba.description: Also flash this VS Code window in the taskbar when VS Code is not focused (Windows)

jeanClaude.notificationSound.onQuestion.description: Alert (sound, notification, taskbar flash) when a Claude Code session needs you: asks for permission, asks a question, or waits for your reply

jeanClaude.notificationSound.onTaskCompl.description: Alert (sound, notification, taskbar flash) when a Claude Code session finishes its reply

jeanClaude.rainbowCsv.enabled.markdownDescription:
Color each column of CSV and TSV files (`.csv`, `.tsv`, `.tab`) in its own color, so the columns are easy to follow. The delimiter (`,` `;` tab `|`) is detected automatically, and quoted fields (including ones spanning several lines) are respected.

You can also turn this on or off by clicking **Jean Claude** in the status bar.

jeanClaude.folderTheme.enabled.markdownDescription:
Give the folder open in this window its own color theme, so windows of different projects are easy to tell apart. Click the palette icon in the status bar (or run **Jean Claude: Set Theme for This Folder**) and pick a theme: it is saved as `workbench.colorTheme` in the folder's `.vscode/settings.json`, so other windows keep their theme.

You can also turn this on or off by clicking **Jean Claude** in the status bar.

jeanClaude.folderTheme.showInStatusBar.description: Show the folder's theme in the status bar (click it to change the theme)
